evidence: test body: `assert commands_main(["session-log", "append", "--", "-dash entry"]) == 0` with no assertion on stored content
Contrast with the comment path which verifies content: `assert _bodies(ticket, rebar_repo) == ["-starts with a dash"]` (test_cli_body_guard.py:138)
The diff it exercises stores content: session_log.py:223 `positionals.extend(argv[index + 1 :])` then session_log.py:254 `append(positionals[0], ...)`
ABSENCE: an append that exits 0 while dropping/mangling '-dash entry' would still pass this test — regression-blind to the silent-loss contract the change targets
advisory.finding: The session-log `--` escape-hatch test asserts only exit code 0 and never verifies the dash-leading entry was actually stored verbatim, leaving the exact 'exits 0 but content silently lost' failure mode (the bug class under review) undetected for the session_log.py `--` path.
scenarios: session_log `_parse_opts`/`append` regresses to drop or truncate the post-`--` entry while still returning 0
advisory.suggested_fix: After the append, read the session log back (e.g. via the same show/read API used elsewhere) and assert the newest entry body == "-dash entry", mirroring the content-verifying comment/tag double-dash tests.
